subject: MAP: cost assumptions & unit-econ checks for pilot
messages:
From: Julia Murphy <julia.murphy@pulsenova.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T15:04:00Z
Subject: MAP: cost assumptions for pilot

Hey Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we pull the MAP together we want to make sure the evaluation plan includes a clear unit-econ sanity check up front so our finance and infra teams can greenlight the pilot. Specific asks from PulseNova:  

- A simple tokens-per-dollar estimate based on an expected prompt/completion mix (we'll provide sample prompt set).
- Clarify caching/prefix assumptions and expected hit rate if we enable prefix caching.
- Batching assumptions for 95th/99th latency cases and how that impacts token economics.
- A short experiment plan (synthetic traffic + one real-user pilot) that demonstrates the numbers.

Can you confirm you can include these items in the MAP and give a rough timeline? We're working to close procurement and would like the MAP (with unit-econ annex) agreed by the end of the month.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Murphy
Product Lead, Integrations
PulseNova

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Julia Murphy <julia.murphy@pulsenova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-10T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions for pilot

Hi Julia —

Appreciate the clear asks. Yes, we can fold a unit-econ annex into the MAP. High level plan:

1) We’ll run two token-econ estimates: a conservative and optimistic case (conservative assumes no prefix cache; optimistic assumes 40–60% effective prefix hit).
2) For batching we’ll provide throughput/latency tradeoffs at three operating points (low, median, peak).
3) Experiment plan: a 72-hour synthetic run with your sample prompt set to validate tokens/sec and hit rates, followed by a 1-week limited-production pilot (50 users) to validate real-world cache behavior.

I’m looping in Ben to own the synthetic-run scripts and Karthik for batching & queueing assumptions. Grace will sketch the acceptance criteria for the MAP annex (what constitutes PASS for unit econ).

Attached a first-pass MAP annex (v0.3) and a quick unit-econ mockup — see the appendix for the numbers I pulled from last week's demo. Can you share the sample prompt set and one-week traffic profile (concurrency, avg tokens per call)? That will let us finalize the numbers.

Proposed timeline: we’ll deliver a draft annex by 2028-11-12 and a finalized MAP for signatures by 2028-11-20, assuming we get the sample data today/tomorrow. Is that workable for you?

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: PulseNova-MAP-v0.3.pdf, PulseNova-unit-econ-mockup.xlsx
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-11T08:46:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: PulseNova MAP — unit-econ playbook & owners

Team —

Taking Julia's asks and my reply above, here are the actions and my suggested assumptions. Please review and flag if you disagree. We need a draft annex by EOD 11/12.

Owners:
- Ben: synthetic-run harness + token accounting (deliver: CSV with tokens/request broken out by prompt vs completion)
- Karthik: batching/latency sim (deliver: sim results for batch sizes 1,4,8,16; 95th/99th latencies; per-token cost impact)
- Grace: acceptance criteria & PASS/FAIL rubric for unit-econ annex (deliver: checklist + go/no-go note)

Assumptions (initial — we'll refine with PulseNova traffic):
- Model: open-variant (LlamaX-13B q4f16) — example throughput numbers used for calc.
- Prompt/completion split: 35% prompt tokens / 65% completion tokens (we'll swap once they send sample set).
- Avg tokens per request (median): 420 tokens (prompt 150 / completion 270).
- Concurrency (expected): 75 concurrent RPS peak; median 18 RPS.
- Caching: prefix caching enabled for deterministic prompts; assume 40% effective prefix hit for optimistic, 15% for conservative. Note: prefix hit = fraction of requests whose prompt prefix is an exact match to a cached key.
- KV cache behavior: warm-start reduces repeated prompt + context recompute; for these checks we model KV hit = prefix hit for simplicity.
- Batching: default batch window 20ms; observed mean batch size at 75 concurrency ~= 6; worst-case (burst) batch size ~= 16.
- Per-token cost sensitivity: quantized model runs give ~3x difference vs fp16; include both in annex.

Proposed experiments (what Ben will run):
1) Synthetic run (72 hours): replay sample prompts at three traffic levels (median, median*2, peak) and capture tokens, latencies, batch distributions, and cache hit rate.
2) Prefetch test: send common prefixes ahead-of-time to create a warmed prefix cache and measure incremental hit improvement.
3) Batching sweep: vary the batch window 5/10/20/50ms to show latency vs tokens/$ tradeoff and pick default for pilot.

Deliverables for draft annex (11/12):
- CSV: tokens/request breakdown + monthlyized tokens/$ projection (conservative & optimistic).
- Batching-latency table and recommended default window.
- Short experiment plan that PulseNova can sign off on.

Open Qs I want you to think about before EOD:
- Are the 420 token median and prompt/completion split reasonable to model? If Ben needs a different default, call it out.
- For prefix caching assumptions, should we model a warmed period (first 24 hours worse) explicitly?
- Karthik — what's the minimal batch-window you think we can force to meet PulseNova's 200ms 95th SLO?

Thanks — ping me in slack if you want to triage.

— Hannah

Attachment referenced: prefetch-batching-experiment-plan.md
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Julia Murphy <julia.murphy@pulsenova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-12T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions for pilot

Julia —

Thanks for the prompt. Per my note below, attached is the MAP annex (v0.3) and the unit-econ mockup. Highlights up front:

- Conservative case (no prefix cache): ~1.9M tokens/day => ~$2,450/day (model-run quantized baseline)
- Optimistic case (40% prefix hit): ~1.2M tokens/day => ~$1,560/day (same quantized baseline)
- Batching impact: moving from batch window 5ms -> 20ms reduces per-token cost by ~14% at your peak profile but increases 95th latency by ~26ms (see table).

As agreed, next steps:
1) Please send the sample prompt set + 7-day concurrency profile by EOD 11/12 so we can finalize the annex numbers.
2) Ben will run the 72-hour synthetic replay once we have the prompt set (target start: 11/14).
3) We will run the prefetch warm-up test during the synthetic run and report back.

If that timeline works I’ll move the annex to v0.4 and add the final CSVs. If you want a tighter conservative buffer for procurement, we can add a delta (20% overhead) to the conservative estimate for billing commitments.

Quick question for your procurement lead: do you need a sample SOW line item with an estimated monthly token commitment (we can provide two bands: conservative/optimistic)?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments: PulseNova-MAP-v0.3.pdf (MAP annex draft), PulseNova-unit-econ-mockup.xlsx (token calculations)
